question: A mobile crane’s outriggers must be fully extended and set unless which condition is true?

options.text: The operator prefers a shorter footprint on a tight site.
options.explanation: Preference is not a chart condition. Short-rigging without the matching chart is overloading the machine.

options.text: The manufacturer’s load chart in use lists that outrigger configuration.
options.explanation: Capacity is only valid for the configuration on the chart in the cab — including outrigger spread.

options.text: The ground looks firm and the lift is under 50% of chart.
options.explanation: Neither ‘looks firm’ nor an arbitrary percentage replaces the published configuration.

options.text: A supervisor has signed a deviation in the FLHA.
options.explanation: A site form cannot raise a crane’s rated capacity or change the OEM configuration rules.

src: REDMC sample · development — OEM chart configuration; WorkSafeBC Part 14

question: Net capacity on a mobile crane is best described as:

options.text: The number printed on the load chart for that radius, with no deductions.
options.explanation: The printed number is gross (or rated) capacity for that configuration — not what you can hang on the hook.

options.text: Gross / rated chart capacity minus required deductions (hook block, rigging, attachments, and other chart deductions).
options.explanation: What you may lift is chart capacity less the deductions the manufacturer requires for that setup.

options.text: The weight of the load only, ignoring the hook and slings.
options.explanation: The crane is holding the load plus everything between the boom and the load.

options.text: Line pull times parts of line, regardless of radius.
options.explanation: Hoist/line capacity is a separate limit. Radius still governs the chart.

question: PARTS OF LINE FORMULA: A 12 000 kg load plus 400 kg of hook and rigging is reeved on 4 parts. Ignoring efficiency losses, line tension is approximately:

options.explanation: That divides the load only and ignores hook and rigging.
Total load = 12 000 + 400 = 12 400 kg. Line tension = 12 400 ÷ 4 = 3 100 kg.
That is the total load, not the tension in each part.
That multiplies instead of dividing by parts of line.

src: REDMC sample · development — Line tension = (load + hook + rigging) ÷ parts of line

question: RIGGING ANGLE MULTIPLIERS: A 4 000 kg load hangs from two slings in a two-leg hitch. The included angle at the hook makes each sling 60° from horizontal. Approximate tension in each sling:

options.explanation: That is the share if the slings were vertical (90°). At 60° from horizontal the multiplier is about 1.15.
Each vertical share is 2 000 kg. At 60° from horizontal, tension ≈ 2 000 × 1.155 ≈ 2 310 kg.
That would be one sling taking the whole load.
The 30° (from horizontal) multiplier is 2.0× — not the 60° case.

question: An anti-two-block (ATB) device is fitted to prevent:

options.text: The boom from exceeding the manufacturer’s maximum angle.
options.explanation: Boom angle / LMI limits are a different function.

options.text: The hook block (or overhaul ball) from contacting the boom tip, which can part the hoist line.
options.explanation: Two-blocking pulls the block into the sheaves. ATB warns or locks out hoist/telescope before that happens.

options.text: The crane from travelling with a load on rubber.
options.explanation: Pick-and-carry is a chart and procedure issue, not ATB.

options.text: Outriggers from retracting under load.
options.explanation: That is a hydraulic / interlock issue, not ATB.

question: Before operating, a mobile crane must be:

options.text: Within 5° of level if the lift is light.
options.explanation: Charts assume the crane is level as the manufacturer specifies. ‘Close enough’ is not a configuration.

options.text: Level within the manufacturer’s tolerance, on a surface that will support the loads.
options.explanation: Level and supporting ground are setup requirements. Out of level cuts capacity and can overturn the crane.

options.text: On a slope if the tires are chocked.
options.explanation: Chocks do not replace level setup or the chart.

options.text: Packed with cribbing under only the high-side outrigger.
options.explanation: You level the crane; you do not leave it out of level and crib one corner as a workaround.

question: POWERLINE RULE: Unless a greater distance is required for the voltage, WorkSafeBC’s basic clearance from overhead lines under 750 V to 75 kV (distribution class) for a mobile crane is treated as:

options.text: A suggestion if the operator can see the lines.
options.explanation: Limits of approach are mandatory. Visibility does not reduce MAD.

options.text: The minimum approach distance in Table 19-1A for that voltage — and you assume lines are live.
options.explanation: Part 19 (and Part 14 for crane work) require the table distances. Higher voltage needs more room. Spotters and limits are controls, not a licence to crowd the line.

options.text: Always 2 ft from any conductor.
options.explanation: 2 ft is not the MAD for power lines.

options.text: Zero if the utility has not returned a call.
options.explanation: No clearance from the utility does not mean the line is safe to work next to.

src: REDMC sample · development — WorkSafeBC Part 19 MAD; confirm Table 19-1A for the voltage on site

question: Pick-and-carry is allowed when:

options.text: The operator has done it before on another make of crane.
options.explanation: Experience on a different machine is not a chart.

options.text: The manufacturer’s chart in use includes that on-rubber / pick-and-carry configuration, and the procedure is followed.
options.explanation: If it is not on the chart, it is not a rated operation.

options.text: The load is under one tonne.
options.explanation: An arbitrary weight is not a configuration.

options.text: Outriggers are 50% extended.
options.explanation: Partial outriggers without a matching chart is not pick-and-carry on rubber, and it is not a rated setup.

src: REDMC sample · development — on-rubber / pick-and-carry only as charted

question: Ground bearing pressure under outrigger floats is reduced by:

options.text: Using smaller floats to concentrate the load.
options.explanation: Smaller area raises pressure. That is the opposite of what you want on weak ground.

options.text: Spreading the load over adequate mats / blocking sized for the float and the ground.
options.explanation: Pressure = force / area. Mats increase area. The ground still has to be able to take that pressure.

options.text: Retracting two outriggers so only two pads carry the crane.
options.explanation: That increases load per pad and is not a rated setup.

options.text: Parking on asphalt because asphalt is always sufficient.
options.explanation: Asphalt, backfill, and vaults fail. You assess the ground; you do not assume the surface.

src: REDMC sample · development — mats increase area; do not invent a site-specific PSF

question: A load moment indicator (LMI / RCL) warning or lockout means:

options.text: The operator may continue if they can see the load is small.
options.explanation: Bypassing an LMI because the load ‘looks light’ is how cranes go over.

options.text: The rated capacity for the current configuration is being approached or exceeded — stop and correct the setup or the lift.
options.explanation: LMI is a limit device for the charted configuration. It is not a substitute for knowing the chart, but you do not work through a lockout.

options.text: The anti-two-block switch has failed.
options.explanation: ATB is a separate device. An LMI alarm is capacity / radius / boom-length related.

options.text: The engine computer needs a regen cycle.
options.explanation: Unrelated to rated capacity.

question: In B.C., Mobile Crane Operator work-based training for the Red Seal apprenticeship is:

options.text: 2,685 hours, same as Tower Crane Operator.
options.explanation: That is the Tower Crane Operator work-based total, not mobile.

options.text: 4,980 hours, including at least 1,600 hours of mobile crane operating time (with 400 hours on specified heavier/lattice equipment).
options.explanation: SkilledTradesBC: 4,980 hours WBT; 1,600 operating hours, of which 400 must be on lattice friction, lattice hydraulic, or hydraulic capacity greater than 80 t.

options.text: 1,000 hours if you already hold a driver’s licence.
options.explanation: A road licence is not crane time.

options.text: No hours if you challenge as a trade qualifier with any crane time.
options.explanation: Trade qualifier still has documented hour requirements. See the SkilledTradesBC program profile.

src: REDMC sample · development — SkilledTradesBC Mobile Crane Operator program profile (July 2024)

question: Standard crane hand signals:

options.text: May be invented on site if everyone on the crew agrees that morning.
options.explanation: Private dialects cause lifts to move when the operator thought they were told to stop.

options.text: Are the standard signals. If the operator cannot see or hear the signal, the crane does not move.
options.explanation: WorkSafeBC Part 14 requires effective communication. Standard signals; stop if the signal is lost.

options.text: Are optional when radios are in use.
options.explanation: Radios still need a protocol. Lost radio is a stop, same as a lost hand signal.

options.text: Are only required for critical lifts.
options.explanation: Every lift needs communication. Critical lifts need more of it, not the first of it.

src: REDMC sample · development — WorkSafeBC Part 14 signals

question: Lattice boom assembly and disassembly must follow:

options.text: The order the truck was loaded, even if that is not the OEM sequence.
options.explanation: Load order is not the assembly procedure. Wrong sequence binds pins and drops sections.

options.text: The manufacturer’s assembly / disassembly procedure for that crane, with the specified blocking, pins, and pendant tension.
options.explanation: Lattice boom A&D is a named, supervised operation. The OEM procedure wins.

options.text: Whatever sequence keeps the boom off the highway fastest.
options.explanation: Speed is not a procedure.

options.text: A generic ‘boom truck’ method if the serial plate is missing.
options.explanation: Missing OEM information is a stop, not a guess.

src: REDMC sample · development — lattice A&D per OEM

question: Wire rope should be removed from service when:

options.text: It looks shiny from use.
options.explanation: Polish is not a rejection criterion.

options.text: It meets the manufacturer’s and applicable standard’s rejection criteria (broken wires, kinks, crushing, corrosion, birdcaging, reduction in diameter).
options.explanation: Inspection criteria are written. Failed rope is out — tagged, isolated, not ‘one more lift’.

options.text: The load is under 50% of chart, even if wires are broken.
options.explanation: Reduced load does not make a rejected rope legal.

options.text: The anti-two-block is working.
options.explanation: ATB does not inspect rope.

src: REDMC sample · development — wire rope rejection; WorkSafeBC Part 15

question: Weather and wind limits for a mobile crane come from:

options.text: The lowest applicable limit — manufacturer, this lift plan, and site — and thunder is a stop.
options.explanation: The lower number wins. Lightning: do not count to 30. Follow the OEM wind table for that boom and load.

options.text: A site custom of ‘we lift until 60 km/h’ for every crane.
options.explanation: A crew habit is not the OEM wind chart.

options.text: Environment Canada warnings only; if there is no warning, there is no limit.
options.explanation: Forecasts help planning. The crane still has a wind table.

options.text: The LMI, which automatically derates for wind.
options.explanation: Most LMIs do not know the wind on the load. Wind is the operator’s and supervisor’s limit.

src: REDMC sample · development — OEM wind / thunderstorm stop

question: The Mobile Crane Operator Red Seal (IP) exam is:

options.text: 100 questions, same as Tower Crane Operator.
options.explanation: Tower Crane Operator IP is 100 questions. Mobile Crane Operator IP is 110.

options.text: 110 four-option questions based on the 2021 RSOS, 70% to pass, no code book.
options.explanation: Official breakdown: A7 B20 C14 D13 E16 F15 G25 = 110. SkilledTradesBC: no code book. 70%.

options.text: Open-book with the manufacturer’s chart supplied as the only reference.
options.explanation: The IP is closed book. Chart items on this practice site are a separate skill, not a claim that Red Seal hands you a Grove chart.

options.text: Level 2 SLE under another name.
options.explanation: There is no Mobile Crane Level 2 SLE. Level 1 SLE, Level 3 SLE, then IP.

src: REDMC sample · development — Red Seal 2021 RSOS exam information; SkilledTradesBC
